_comment: Ankle-foot rehab corridor (post-sprain, Achilles tendinopathy, plantar fasciitis) — ROM through banded strengthening to balance, gait, and eccentric loading. Authored in-house: original instruction text, mechanics are facts, phrasing is ours. heel-raise and ankle-pumps live in the knee corridor and are deliberately not duplicated here. The foot-intrinsics group (toe spreading, toe yoga, short-foot, marble pickup, loaded towel scrunch) is seated so it stays available while weight bearing is restricted; the standing short-foot is the one that loads the foot, and the edges leading to it say standing must be cleared first.

exercises.name: Ankle Alphabet
instructions: Sit tall in a chair and extend your working leg so the foot hovers just above the floor.
Keeping the leg itself still, trace the letters of the alphabet in the air with your big toe, moving only at the ankle.
Make each letter large enough to reach the comfortable edge of your motion in every direction.
If a letter pinches or sharply pulls, draw it smaller — a gentle stretch is fine, sharp pain is not.

exercises.name: Towel Scrunch
instructions: Sit in a chair with a towel spread flat on a smooth floor and your bare foot resting on the near edge.
Keeping the heel planted, scrunch your toes to gather the towel in toward you, a little at a time.
When you run out of towel, smooth it back out and begin again.
If the arch of your foot cramps, pause and gently stretch the toes back before continuing.

exercises.name: Wall Calf Stretch
instructions: Stand facing a wall with both hands on it at about chest height.
Step your working leg well back, heel flat and toes pointing straight at the wall.
Keeping that back knee straight, bend the front knee and lean toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the upper calf.
Keep the back heel pressed to the floor the whole time — if it lifts, shorten your stance.
Hold steady without bouncing; the stretch should feel firm but never sharp.

exercises.name: Soleus Stretch
instructions: Stand facing a wall in the same staggered stance as the calf stretch, hands on the wall.
This time bend the back knee slightly while keeping that heel flat on the floor.
Sink your weight down and forward until you feel a deeper, lower stretch just above the heel.
Hold steady and keep breathing — no bouncing, and the heel never leaves the floor.

exercises.name: Band Dorsiflexion
instructions: Sit on the floor or a bed with your working leg straight out in front of you.
Loop a resistance band over the top of your foot and anchor the far end to something sturdy ahead of you, so the band pulls the foot away.
Pull your foot up toward your shin against the band, moving only at the ankle.
Pause at the top, then let the band draw the foot back down slowly — the return should be just as controlled as the pull.

exercises.name: Band Plantarflexion
instructions: Sit on the floor or a bed with your working leg straight and a band looped around the ball of that foot, holding an end in each hand.
Press the foot down and away, like pushing a gas pedal, until you reach a comfortable end range.
Keep the knee still — the movement comes from the ankle alone.
Return slowly, resisting the band on the way back rather than letting it snap the foot up.

exercises.name: Band Inversion & Eversion
instructions: Sit with your working leg straight and a resistance band looped around the forefoot, anchored out to one side.
Keeping the knee pointing at the ceiling, steer the foot away from the anchor — sweeping inward across your midline — then return with control.
Re-anchor the band on the other side and steer the foot outward the same way.
Steer from the ankle, not the hip: the knee should barely move.
Slow and controlled beats big and fast in both directions.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance
instructions: Stand beside a wall or counter so support is within easy reach.
Shift your weight onto the working leg and lift the other foot just off the floor.
Stand tall with a soft knee and let the foot make small corrections — that quiet wobble is the exercise.
Touch the support the moment you need it; a fingertip is enough.
To progress, stand on a balance pad or repeat the drill with your eyes closed, support close by.

exercises.name: Heel-and-Toe Walks
instructions: Stand at one end of a clear hallway, beside a wall or counter you can touch if needed.
Walk forward on your heels with the toes lifted, taking short steps and staying tall through the trunk.
At the end, turn and walk back up on the balls of your feet with the heels high.
Alternate heel walking and toe walking for the whole time; a steady rhythm matters more than speed.

exercises.name: Eccentric Heel Drop
instructions: Stand with the balls of both feet on the edge of a step, heels hanging free, one hand on the rail or wall for balance.
Rise up onto your toes using both legs together.
Lift the healthy foot away and lower slowly on the working leg alone, letting the heel sink just below the level of the step.
Place the other foot back down and rise with both legs again — never push up on the working leg alone.
The slow lowering is the exercise; mild soreness in the tendon is acceptable, sharp pain means stop.

exercises.name: Toe Spreading
instructions: Sit tall in a chair with your bare foot resting on the floor — resting only, with no weight sent down through it.
Without curling the toes under or lifting the heel, spread your toes as wide apart as you can, like opening a fan.
Hold the spread steady while you breathe normally, then let the toes relax completely.
If the toes won't separate at first, ease them apart with your fingers a few times and then try again on your own.
If the arch of your foot cramps, rest it and gently stretch the toes back before the next hold.

exercises.name: Toe Yoga (Big Toe Lift & Press)
instructions: Sit tall with your bare foot resting flat on the floor, heel and ball of the foot down.
Lift only your big toe toward the ceiling while the other four toes stay pressed to the floor.
Lower the big toe and press it firmly down, then lift the other four toes while the big toe stays down.
Move slowly. It is normal for this to feel awkward at first — if the toes won't separate, lift them all together and work toward lifting one at a time.
Keep the heel down and the ankle still for the whole set.

exercises.name: Short-Foot (Arch Doming), Seated
instructions: Sit tall with your bare foot resting flat on the floor and your knee bent to roughly a right angle.
Without curling your toes, draw the ball of your foot back toward your heel so the arch lifts into a gentle dome, as if shortening the foot.
Keep the toes long and relaxed, with the big toe, little toe and heel all staying in light contact with the floor.
Hold the dome while you breathe normally, then release.
The movement is small. If the toes claw or the arch cramps, ease off — a gentle, controlled dome is the goal.

exercises.name: Marble Pickup
instructions: Sit in a chair with about ten marbles on the floor in front of you and a bowl beside them. Cotton balls or crumpled tissue work too.
Using only your toes, grip one marble, lift it, and carry it over to the bowl.
Let it drop into the bowl, then go back for the next one until the marbles have all moved.
Keep the heel resting down and let the toes do the work; slow and deliberate beats fast.
If your toes cramp, stop and spread them wide for a few seconds before carrying on.

exercises.name: Loaded Towel Scrunch
instructions: Sit in a chair with a towel spread flat on a smooth floor, your bare foot at the near edge, and a light weight — a full water bottle or a can of soup — on the far end of the towel.
Keeping your heel resting down, scrunch your toes to drag the towel toward you, pulling the weight along with it.
When the weight reaches your foot, smooth the towel back out and slide the weight to the far end to start again.
Stay with a light weight; your PT will tell you when to change it.
If the arch of your foot cramps, pause and gently stretch the toes back before continuing.

exercises.name: Short-Foot, Standing
instructions: Stand barefoot beside a wall or counter you can touch, with your weight spread evenly across both feet.
Without curling your toes, draw the ball of the working foot back toward the heel so the arch lifts into a gentle dome.
Keep the big toe, little toe and heel pressing evenly into the floor, with the knee soft and still.
Hold the dome while you breathe normally, then relax; touch the wall whenever you need it.
If the toes claw or the arch cramps, ease off — a gentle dome held steadily is the goal.

progressions.note: Add resistance once the full alphabet traces twice through without pinching at any letter.
Add the steering directions once the pull-up stays smooth through the band's full stretch, including the slow return.
Begin balance work when both steering directions stay controlled without the knee drifting to help.
Progress when the whole towel gathers in without the heel lifting or the arch cramping.
Move to step loading once full-range presses against a medium band stay controlled both ways with no next-day calf soreness.
Add the bent-knee version once the straight-knee stretch gives only a gentle pull at end range with the heel flat.
Start eccentric loading once both stretch positions are comfortable with the heel staying flat throughout the hold.
Progress when a full minute of steady single-leg standing on firm ground needs no touch of the support.
Add the lift-and-press once all five toes spread evenly and hold without curling under.
Add the arch dome once the big toe lifts and presses on its own while the other four stay quietly down.
Move to standing once the seated dome holds steady for the full count with the toes staying relaxed, and standing is cleared.
Begin single-leg balance once the standing dome holds without the toes clawing or the arch collapsing.
Add the pickups once the towel gathers in smoothly with the arch staying relaxed throughout.
Add resistance once every marble moves across without a drop and without the arch cramping.
Move to the standing dome once the weighted pull stays smooth and cramp-free for the full set, and standing is cleared.
